limitations: Only the lift source is an actual native observation. All post-yaw/transport/fresh states are frozen rigid-grasp hypotheses.
Rotating a saved teddy does not predict deformable grasp settling, slip, contact forces, or the final dynamic orientation.
Geometry extents and all-tetra section envelopes do not certify passage through deforming cloth or handles.
No source, default or trial config is changed; no additional angles or offsets are searched.
Native force, torque, J, strain, held material, release eligibility and final whole-teddy containment remain required.
Frozen rigid-grasp rotation does not predict soft deformation, slip, force, or eventual insertion.
Joint position and rate bounds cover the continuous reference spline; rigid robot clearances and FK errors are sampled.
The left arm is checked at actual and commanded static poses; motion between these poses or native compliance is not certified.
Finger geometry uses measured individual fingers for frozen left solids and paired means for robot clearance. The runner retains finite-force grasp motor targets.
Analytic bounds are evaluated in double precision with explicit padding, not directed-rounding interval arithmetic.
Native force/torque/grip/deformation/table gates remain mandatory; no task-success claim follows.

frozen_bear_left_rotation_sweep.scope: Continuous ideal WORLD-Z rigid frozen-teddy arc about measured fixed TCP, against both static left poses. No dynamic or continuous joint-FK tracking certificate.

hypothetical_construction.left_arm_pose_scope: Saved commanded endpoint; original measured left fingers retained. Not an actual native endpoint.
